lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Didn't see a thing. I close late, open early, no time to look sideways.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You know Mark, the one who hangs around here?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: The crazy one? I know him. Wouldn't trust him to tell me the time of day.
She says it without malice, with the tiredness of someone who decided long ago which words are worth listening to.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Carla used to come in for coffee alone. Always sitting by the window, like she was waiting for someone who never showed.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Did she mention having trouble with anyone at the motel?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Nobody around here speaks ill of Robert Hale, detective. And when a whole town won't dare criticize a man... that's exactly when you should be most suspicious.
She wipes the cup with a dry rag and doesn't add another word.
Marta flips the sign on the door, but doesn't kick me out.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Carla would come by late, sometimes. When there was nobody else left. She said she felt safe here.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Safe from what, exactly?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: She never said it in so many words. But you learn to read it, when someone checks the door every two minutes.
She switches off the coffee maker. The conversation, for today, is over.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Coffee, detective? On the house today.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: That's new.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Carla never let me pay her back for anything either. Kept saying 'someday, when I'm in Seattle, I'll send you a postcard and we'll call it even.'
Marta sets the cup down without meeting my eyes. There won't be a postcard now, and we both know it.

topics.displayName: Ask her what she meant about Robert

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You said to be suspicious when nobody criticizes a man. Was that about Robert?
She takes a long moment before answering, glancing at the door like she's calculating who might be listening.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: I didn't say any names, detective. But Carla stopped coming in smiling about a month before she died. And she started carrying that bag everywhere, like she couldn't bear to put it down.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: That's all I can tell you without my voice shaking.
